evidence.claim: A retired workflow id remains resolvable and returns the successor: resolve('wf.catalog-class.discovery-only').successor_id == 'wf.catalog-class.typed-restore'.
A consumer pinned to the retired id still executes (no hard break) and emits typed warning WORKFLOW_SUPERSEDED naming successor 'wf.catalog-class.typed-restore'.
Deletion of a referenced workflow is refused; the id still resolves afterwards (FC-11347: retirement is never silent removal).
Retirement schema admits only SUPERSESSION (successor+migration) or DEPRECATION (reason+removal_date); DELETION and dangling successors are rejected.

probes.command: validate_retirement rejects DELETION / missing successor / missing migration

negative_controls.description: Dropping the retired body without a retirement record (silent deletion) must make resolve and pinned execute hard-break. The public delete() path must not do this.
negative_controls.good_state_output: supersede+pin execute ok; delete refused; still resolvable

negative_controls.description: Malformed retirement records must be SCHEMA_INVALID.

residual_unknowns.claim: IMP-0203 (certification record) is a catalog dependency and is not delivered on this worktree; retirement does not consult certificates.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Re-run resolve against a catalog that also holds IMP-0203 certificates.

reviewer.notes: probe2 is a separate process that did not author retirement.py; it re-runs delete-refusal and the silent-deletion mutant.
